patients.label: Case 1: 57-year-old woman with Alzheimer disease and later myoclonus (Group 1)

identity_evidence.quote: A 57-year-old female with a three-year history of cognitive decline presented with recent-onset myoclonic jerks in the upper extremities.

patients.label: Case 2: 70-year-old man with Alzheimer disease and myoclonic jerks (Group 1)

identity_evidence.quote: A 70-year-old male with a 2.5-year history of cognitive and behavioral impairment presented with myoclonic jerks affecting all extremities and the face.

patients.label: Case 3: 61-year-old woman with Alzheimer disease and later distal upper extremity myoclonus (Group 1)

identity_evidence.quote: A 61-year-old female presented with a six-year history of progressive memory loss and behavioral changes.

patients.label: Case 4: 62-year-old man with Alzheimer disease and episodic speech disturbance (Group 1)

identity_evidence.quote: A 62-year-old male with a one-year history of mild memory issues and episodic speech disturbance underwent evaluation.

patients.label: Case 5: 67-year-old woman with logopenic-variant Alzheimer disease, myoclonus and non-convulsive status epilepticus (Group 1)

identity_evidence.quote: A 67-year-old female presented with speech and memory complaints.

patients.label: Case 6: 88-year-old woman with long-standing Alzheimer disease and focal impaired awareness seizures (Group 1)

identity_evidence.quote: An 88-year-old female with long-standing AD presented following three episodes of unresponsiveness, head turning, mouth automatisms, and staring.

attribution_limitations: Follow-up duration is printed as a one-year follow-up in the case text and as 10 months in Table 1. A one-year figure may be a rounding of 10 months, so this is recorded as an ambiguity; both values are kept review-only and no value is chosen.

patients.label: Case 7: 65-year-old man with known epilepsy on valproate presenting after a fall, later diagnosed with Alzheimer disease (Group 2)

identity_evidence.quote: A 65-year-old male with a known epilepsy diagnosis, treated with valproate, presented following a fall.

patients.label: Case 8: 72-year-old woman presenting to the emergency department with status epilepticus, diagnosed with mild cognitive impairment in the context of epilepsy (Group 2)

identity_evidence.quote: A 72-year-old female presented to the emergency department with status epilepticus, successfully managed with intravenous diazepam and phenytoin.

patients.label: Case 9: 52-year-old man with chronic epilepsy and attention lapses, diagnosed with mild cognitive impairment (Group 2)

identity_evidence.quote: A 52-year-old male with chronic epilepsy presumed secondary to prior encephalitis presented with attention lapses.

attribution_limitations: Follow-up duration differs: the text reports a six-year follow-up and Table 1 prints 228 months. Both are kept review-only; no reconciliation or definition of follow-up is inferred.

patients.label: Case 10: 64-year-old woman with memory impairment and prior seizure, diagnosed with mild cognitive impairment and later Alzheimer disease pathology (Group 2)

identity_evidence.quote: A 64-year-old female presented with memory impairment, sleep disturbances, and transient episodes with mild confusion.

attribution_limitations: ACE-R score is printed as 78 in the case text and 76 in Table 1 (one-character difference). Both are kept review-only; no value is chosen.

The Discussion lists the first seizure of patient 10 as 19 months earlier (relative to the MCI diagnosis), while the case text places the seizure 18 months before presentation. The reference points may differ and the values differ by one character; the Discussion value is kept review-only and the case-text value is not changed.
The case text says poor tolerance prompted lacosamide but does not name the drug that was poorly tolerated; no drug is inferred.

patients.label: Case 11: 74-year-old woman with an episode of altered consciousness, diagnosed with focal impaired awareness seizures of left temporal origin and mild cognitive impairment (Group 2)

identity_evidence.quote: A 74-year-old female presented with an episode of altered consciousness lasting eight minutes, during which she was unresponsive and staring.

patients.label: Case 12: 63-year-old woman with three years of memory, speech and behavioral impairment and prior unmedicated seizures, diagnosed with Alzheimer disease (Group 2)

identity_evidence.quote: A 63-year-old female presented with three years of memory, speech, and behavioral impairment and a history of prior unmedicated epileptic seizures.

patients.label: Case 13: 70-year-old man initially diagnosed with mild cognitive impairment who later developed episodes of unresponsiveness and was diagnosed with focal impaired awareness seizures of left temporal origin (Group 2)

identity_evidence.quote: A 70-year-old male was initially diagnosed with MCI.

attribution_limitations: The Discussion says MCI was diagnosed at the time of evaluation for the first epileptic episode for patients 11 and 13, whereas the case text diagnoses MCI first and describes the episodes two years later. No reconciliation is inferred.

The Discussion says the MRI abnormalities and cognitive performance "stabilized" after antiseizure medication, whereas the Results say the MRI abnormality was resolved; only the Results wording is recorded as the MRI finding.

Table 1 prints a single untimed ACE-R score for patient 13, while the case text reports two scores at different times (83 at the initial MCI diagnosis and 71 six months after treatment). The table value is kept review-only and not assigned to either time point.

patients.label: Case 14: 68-year-old man with a recent seizure treated with levetiracetam and a second episode of transient loss of consciousness, diagnosed with Alzheimer disease in the context of temporal epilepsy (Group 2)

identity_evidence.quote: A 68-year-old male with a history of levetiracetam treatment after an epileptic seizure 3 months earlier presented after a second episode of transient loss of consciousness lasting 10 min, without overt convulsions or other motor phenomena.

events.description: Presentation with myoclonic jerks, examination, first EEG, ACE-R and SPECT

evidence.quote: A 57-year-old female with a three-year history of cognitive decline presented with recent-onset myoclonic jerks in the upper extremities. Neurological examination revealed brisk deep tendon reflexes (DTRs), a positive grasp reflex, apraxia in the upper extremities, alexia, agraphia, and visuospatial impairment. EEG demonstrated generalized background slowing (8 Hz) without focal abnormalities. The ACE-R score was 38, rCBF SPECT supported an AD diagnosis, and rivastigmine was initiated.

evidence.quote: A 57-year-old female with a three-year history of cognitive decline presented with recent-onset myoclonic jerks in the upper extremities. Neurological examination revealed brisk deep tendon reflexes (DTRs), a positive grasp reflex, apraxia in the upper extremities, alexia, agraphia, and visuospatial impairment. EEG demonstrated generalized background slowing (8 Hz) without focal abnormalities. The ACE-R score was 38, rCBF SPECT supported an AD diagnosis, and rivastigmine was initiated.

events.description: Presentation with myoclonic jerks, examination, ACE-R, MRI and EEG

evidence.quote: A 70-year-old male with a 2.5-year history of cognitive and behavioral impairment presented with myoclonic jerks affecting all extremities and the face. Neurological examination demonstrated brisk DTRs and positive primitive reflexes. ACE-R score was 44. Brain MRI revealed parietal atrophy, while EEG showed slow wave activity and rare complexes of slow spike-wave discharges (2–2.5 Hz) predominantly in the right posterior regions (Figure 2A). Myoclonic jerks corresponded to muscle artifacts (followed by slow waves in the EEG) without identifiable spike anomalies on EEG (Figure 2B).

evidence.quote: A 61-year-old female presented with a six-year history of progressive memory loss and behavioral changes.
